item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
831
ABPZ20 KNHC 272336
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Thu Aug 27 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on newly formed
Tropical Storm Karina, located well south of the southern tip of the
Baja California Peninsula, as well as newly formed Tropical Storm
Lowell, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lala, located several
hundred miles north of Kure Atoll.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form this weekend well to the
south of southwestern Mexico. Environmental conditions appear
favorable for gradual development of this system, and a tropical
depression is likely to form early next week while it moves
west-northwestward to northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands over the weekend or early next week. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well offshore of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Karina are issued under WMO
header WTPZ31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP1.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Karina are issued under WMO
header WTPZ21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP1.

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Lowell are issued under WMO
header WTPZ32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP2.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Lowell are issued under WMO
header WTPZ22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP2.

----------------------------------------------

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1000 MB...29.53 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM MST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Karina was
located near latitude 11.9 North, longitude 112.7 West. Karina is
moving toward the west-northwest near 13 mph (20 km/h) and this
general motion is expected to continue over the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 50 mph (85 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Strengthening is expected to continue as Karina 
is forecast to become a hurricane over the weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles (335 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1000 mb (29.53 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Tropical Storm Karina will begin to
affect portions of the coast of southwest Mexico and the Baja
California Peninsula this weekend.  These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.  Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Zelinsky

item.title: Tropical Storm Karina Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM MST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 280244
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Karina Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
800 PM MST Thu Aug 27 2026

Tropical Storm Karina has gradually strengthened since the last 
advisory, indicated by the most recent subjective Dvorak estimate of 
T3.0/45 kt from TAFB, and the objective estimates from UW-CIMSS 
sitting around 35 to 45 kt. Latest satellite imagery continues to 
display relatively well-organized convection surrounding the center 
of Karina, with a slightly elongated circulation in place. Given the 
above, the NHC initial intensity has been increased to 45 kt.
 
Karina's initial motion estimate has altered a bit from the previous 
advisory as well, now set at 315/11 kt. This heading is forecast to 
prevail through the next several days as mid- to upper-level ridging 
centered over much of the southwestern US will dictate Karina's 
motion prior to the intervention of an upper-level trough by early 
next week. Because of this interaction, and as showcased by model 
guidance, particularly GDMI and HCCA, Karina's track will begin to 
steer more westward. The reliable guidance remains in good 
agreement on the track of Karina, with confidence decreasing as 
model spread increases toward the latter end of the forecast early 
next week.
 
Guidance provided by the ECMWF SHIPS indicates that Karina remains 
in a favorable environment for steady intensification over the next 
several days as Karina is forecast to move through a moisture-laden 
area with low shear. SHIPS-RII consensus guidance suggests a 
nearly 60 percent chance of a 55 kt increase in winds over the next 
48 hours; a 10 percent increase from the previous advisory. In 
fact, the latest guidance from Google DeepMind indicates a 60 
percent chance that Karina becomes a major hurricane by early next 
week. However, it is important to note that given Karina currently 
lacks a tight inner core, the NHC forecast reflects a slower 
intensification rate. Conversely, if an inner core is established 
sooner, Karina could intensify much quicker than forecast. Karina 
is forecast to transition into a more stable environment and begin 
weakening by day 5.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lowell Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
335 
WTPZ42 KNHC 280248
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Lowell Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP122026
500 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
Satellite imagery shows a large area of deep convection that has
been persisting with Lowell, with a ball of deep convection near and
over the center, and a curved band noted as well.  A 27/2204Z AMSR-2
pass also shows the same curved banding pattern.  Earlier
scatterometer data showed that the center was slightly elongated,
with tropical-storm-force winds confined to the southern semicircle
and a radius of maximum wind (RMW) of about 50 n mi.  The latest
TAFB Dvorak classification is T2.5/35 kt and objective estimates
have been ranging from 30-42 kt.  The initial intensity is held at
35 kt for this advisory, but given the impressive banding and
maintenance of deep convection, this estimate could be slightly
conservative.
 
The initial motion estimate remains slowly east-northeastward, or 70
degrees at 4 kt.  A slow counterclockwise turn toward the north and
then the west is expected over the next 36 h as ridging builds in
to the northeast and north.  A generally westward to
west-northwestward motion should then continue for the rest of the
forecast period.  There remains a ton of spread in the forward speed
from 72 to 120 h, which could be related to Karina's location and
size, relative to Lowell's.  The NHC track is a little faster toward
the west than the previous forecast beyond 36 hours, but not nearly
as fast as the HCCA and GDMI.
 
Lowell will be over relatively favorable environmental conditions
for the next 5 days, with warm sea-surface temperatures, light to
moderate easterly wind shear and relatively moist air.  Despite
these favorable conditions, it is a bit perplexing that the models
are so slow to strengthen Lowell to a hurricane.  Perhaps the slow
strengthening at first could be due to the large RMW observed on
the previous ASCAT pass along with the moderate easterly shear.  If
the cyclone is able to gain enough latitude and get north of 13N,
it should find itself in a more favorable upper-level environment,
which could allow for more significant strengthening in a few days.
Little change has been made to the previous NHC intensity forecast
in the first 4 days, but a higher intensity is shown at day 5.  The
NHC intensity forecast is higher than the intensity consensus, but
not as high as the HMON and HCCA, which bring Lowell to major
hurricane strength by day 5.  The confidence in the intensity
forecast is below average, and it is possible that Lowell could
strengthen more than forecast.
